analysis: Spectra of symmetric-difference (Seidel), strong (A+I), co-normal (J-A) and Cartesian (A) products obtained from the factors agree with direct diagonalisation to relative error 1.2e-14 in all 16 cases (n = m <= 40); at nm = 1600 the factor route took about 0.2-0.4 ms against 14-19 s for numpy.linalg.eigvalsh on the shared, heavily loaded machine (absolute times inflated by load; the gain is the standard Kronecker O((nm)^3) -> O(n^3 + m^3 + nm log nm)).
assumptions: Erdos-Renyi G(n, 1/2) factors with n = m in {10, 20, 30, 40} (seeded)
baseline: numpy.linalg.eigvalsh on the full (nm x nm) matrix
timings are machine-dependent and stored under 'timings' (excluded from the result hash)
falsification: Max deviation above 1e-8 * spectral norm, or no speed-up at nm = 1600.

history.new: Spectra of symmetric-difference (Seidel), strong (A+I), co-normal (J-A) and Cartesian (A) products obtained from the factors agree with direct diagonalisation to relative error 1.2e-14 in all 16 cases (n = m <= 40); at nm = 1600 the factor route took about 0.2-0.4 ms against 14-19 s for numpy.linalg.eigvalsh on the shared, heavily loaded machine (absolute times inflated by load; the gain is the standard Kronecker O((nm)^3) -> O(n^3 + m^3 + nm log nm)).

hypothesis: The factor route is exact up to rounding (max error < 1e-8 relative to the spectral norm) and asymptotically faster (O(n^3 + m^3 + nm log nm) vs O((nm)^3)); this is the standard Kronecker eigenvalue speed-up, newly applicable to the symmetric-difference product via Seidel matrices.
methodology: XOR: Seidel spectrum = {(s+1)(t+1) - 1}; strong: adjacency spectrum = {(a+1)(b+1) - 1}; co-normal: spectrum of J - A multiplies; Cartesian: adjacency spectrum = {a + b}. Compare sorted spectra and wall-clock times (median of 3).
question: How much faster and how accurate is it to obtain the spectrum of a product graph from its factors via the Kronecker characters (Theorems 4-6) instead of diagonalising the product matrix?

summary: max relative spectral error over 16 cases: 1.2e-14 (< 1e-8: True)
